pages.title: What this unit is about
pages.body:
> 🌐 **Strand 3 — Communication Networks**
Sub-strand 2: Internet and Social Media

Social media and email have changed how people communicate, learn and do business. In this unit you will identify types of social media, use them wisely, and master the features of electronic mail, including attachments, the address book, and the From, To, Cc, Bcc and Subject fields.

pages.title: Content standard and lessons
pages.body:
> 🎯 **Content standard**
- **B7.3.2.1** Demonstrate the use of social networking and electronic mail.

> 🧭 **What you will be able to do**
- **B7.3.2.1.1** Identify the various types and uses of social media sites such as those for social networking (Facebook, LinkedIn, WhatsApp) and microblogging (Twitter, Tumblr).
- **B7.3.2.1.2** Demonstrate the use of the following features of electronic mail: attachment and address book.

> 🗺️ **Lessons in this unit**
- 8.1 Social Networking and Microblogging
- 8.2 Electronic Mail: Attachments and the Address Book

**Core competencies developed:** Creativity and Innovation (CI6.3), Digital Literacy (DL6.3).

pages.title: Social Networking and Microblogging
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B7.3.2.1.1
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- define social media;
- identify types of social media sites;
- illustrate the uses of social networking and microblogging platforms;
- use social media responsibly.
**Social media** are websites and apps that let people **create, share and interact with content** and with each other online. Social media sites can be grouped by their main purpose.
## Social networking sites
**Social networking** sites help people build and maintain connections with friends, family, classmates, colleagues and communities.
| **Platform** | **Main use** | **Example of good use** |
|---|---|---|
| Facebook | Connecting with friends and family; sharing posts, photos and videos; groups and pages; events; Marketplace | A school’s Old Students’ Association page announcing a fundraising event |
| WhatsApp | Instant messaging, voice and video calls, groups, communities, channels and status updates; end-to-end encrypted | A class WhatsApp group (with parents and teachers) for homework reminders |
| LinkedIn | Professional networking: CVs (profiles), job searches, business news, professional groups | A graduate connecting with employers and applying for internships |
## Microblogging sites
**Microblogging** means posting **short** messages, images or links frequently to followers. Posts are often grouped by **hashtags** (e.g. #GhanaDecides, #BECE2026).

pages.title: Social Networking and Microblogging (continued)
pages.body:
| **Platform** | **Main use** |
|---|---|
| X (formerly Twitter) | Short public posts (“posts”, formerly “tweets”), news updates, following public figures and organisations, trending topics. Twitter was renamed **X** in 2023. |
| Tumblr | Short blog posts mixing text, images, GIFs and videos; reblogging content from others |
| Threads, Bluesky | Newer microblogging platforms similar to X |
> 🪜 **Step by step — Demonstration: creating a safe post on a microblogging platform (teacher-led)**
1. Sign in to the class account managed by your teacher (most platforms require users to be at least **13 years old**).
2. Click **Post** (or **New post**). Type a short message, e.g. “B7 Gold learned about network topologies today! #ComputingGH”.
3. Add an image if appropriate, check spelling and make sure the post reveals no private information.
4. Click **Post**. Observe how followers can **like**, **reply**, **repost** and **share** it.
## Uses of social media
- Communication with family and friends, locally and abroad.
- Sharing news and information quickly (e.g. weather alerts, school announcements).
- Learning: educational videos, study groups, following experts.
- Business: advertising, selling online, customer service.
- Finding jobs and professional networking (LinkedIn).
- Mobilising communities for causes (clean-up campaigns, blood donation).

pages.title: Social Networking and Microblogging (continued)
pages.body:
> 🛡️ **Safety first — Be a responsible social media user**
- Respect the **minimum age** rules of each platform.
- Never share passwords, your home address, school location in real time, or your Ghana Card number.
- Think before you post: posts can last forever and be screenshotted.
- Do not share fake news; check facts first.
- Be kind: no bullying, insults or hateful content.
- Report abuse and tell a trusted adult. In Ghana you can also contact the **Cyber Security Authority** (call or text **292**).

pages.title: Electronic Mail: Attachments and the Address Book
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B7.3.2.1.2
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- create, send and receive email;
- reply to and forward email;
- explain and use the From, To, Cc, Bcc and Subject fields;
- attach files and use the address book.
**Electronic mail (email)** is a way of sending messages and files from one person to another over the Internet. Popular email services include **Gmail**, **Outlook.com** and **Yahoo Mail**. An **email address** has the form username@domain, for example ama.owusu@gmail.com.
| **Part of the address** | **Example** | **Meaning** |
|---|---|---|
| Username | ama.owusu | Identifies the person or account |
| @ (“at”) | @ | Separates the user from the domain |
| Domain name | gmail.com | The email provider or organisation |
[[fig:c7-f18|Figure 17: The parts of a new email message]]

pages.title: The header fields of an email
pages.body:
## The header fields of an email
| **Field** | **Purpose** | **Reason for using it** |
|---|---|---|
| From: | The sender’s address (filled in automatically) | Shows the receiver who sent the message |
| To: | The main recipient(s) | The people who must read and act on the message |
| Cc: (carbon copy) | Sends a copy to others; **all recipients can see** Cc addresses | To keep someone informed, e.g. copying your class teacher on a message to the headteacher |
| Bcc: (blind carbon copy) | Sends a copy, but **Bcc addresses are hidden** from all other recipients | To protect privacy when emailing many people (e.g. all parents) or to inform someone discreetly |
| Subject: | A short summary of the message | Helps the receiver know what the email is about and find it later |
| Body | The main message | Should be polite, clear and well organised |
| Attachment | A file sent with the email | To send documents, photos, presentations, etc. |
> 🪜 **Step by step — Creating and sending an email (Gmail)**
1. Open a web browser, go to mail.google.com and sign in.
2. Click **Compose**. A **New Message** window opens.
3. In **To**, type the recipient’s address. Click **Cc** or **Bcc** to show those fields if needed.
4. Type a clear **Subject**, e.g. “B7 Gold – E-waste project report (Group 3)”.
5. Type the message in the body: greeting, message, closing and your name.
6. To **attach a file**, click the **paper-clip** (Attach files) icon, find the file on your computer, select it and click **Open**. Wait until the upload finishes. (Gmail allows up to **25 MB** of attachments per email; larger files are shared as a Google Drive link.)
7. Check everything, then click **Send**.

pages.title: The header fields of an email (continued)
pages.body:
> 🪜 **Step by step — Receiving, replying to and forwarding email**
1. New messages appear in the **Inbox**; unread messages are shown in **bold**. Click a message to open it.
2. To open or save an attachment, click it or click the **Download** arrow. Only open attachments you were expecting from people you trust.
3. Click **Reply** to answer only the sender. The subject begins with **Re:**.
4. Click **Forward** to send the message (and its attachments) to someone else. The subject begins with **Fwd:**. Add a note explaining why you are forwarding it.
## The address book (Contacts)
The **address book** (called **Contacts** in Gmail and **People** in Outlook) stores the names, email addresses and phone numbers of people you communicate with, so you don’t need to remember their addresses. When you start typing a name in the **To** field, the address is suggested automatically. You can also create **groups (labels)** such as “B7 Gold Parents” to email many people at once.
> 🪜 **Step by step — Adding a contact in Gmail**
1. Click the **Google apps** grid (top right) › **Contacts**, or go to contacts.google.com.
2. Click **Create contact**.
3. Type the first name, surname, email address and phone number, then click **Save**.
4. To create a group, select contacts, click the **label** icon and create a new label, e.g. Computing Club.

pages.title: The header fields of an email (continued)
pages.body:
> 🎯 **BECE focus — Email etiquette (netiquette)**
- Use a clear subject line.
- Begin with a greeting and end with your name.
- Do not type in ALL CAPITALS (it looks like shouting).
- Keep messages short and polite; check spelling before sending.
- Use **Bcc** when emailing a large group to protect their addresses.
- Do not forward chain letters or open suspicious attachments.
> 💻 **Practical session — Email exercise**
1. Create a school or personal email account with your teacher’s guidance (or use a class account).
2. Add three classmates to your address book.
3. Send your teacher an email with your word-processed notice from Unit 4 as an attachment, **Cc** your group leader, and use a suitable subject.
4. Reply to the email you receive from a classmate, then forward it to another classmate with a short note.

pages.title: Review: written and practical tasks
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Review exercises** — answer these in your exercise book or on the computer, then check with your teacher.
## Short answer questions
1. Distinguish between social networking and microblogging, giving **two** examples of each.
2. State **four** uses of social media in Ghana.
3. Explain the difference between Cc and Bcc, and give a situation in which you would use each.
4. Describe the steps to attach a file to an email.
5. List **five** rules of email etiquette.
